22.7. A page whose subsections are bold paragraphs

The prose above the first heading, which has no heading to be named by and stays the page preamble.

7.1 Ownership of the trade mark

An applicant must be the owner of the trade mark.

7.1.1 Joint owners

Two or more people may apply jointly.

7.1.2

An unnamed subsection still holds its prose.

Suggested Alternatives

A bold line the Manual uses as a label, not as a section.

6.4 A number belonging to another page

Left in the prose, because a heading whose number contradicts its page is not something to resolve.

7.2 A bolded opening and then the sentence continues without emphasis.

7.15% of applications are affected

7.3 A heading with no paragraph wrapper

The wrapper is incidental; the emphasis is the assertion.

7.3(a) A paragraph letter

Nested under 7.3 rather than beside it.
